lessons.title: Pediatric Systematic Assessment: PAT → ABCDE → SAMPLE
lessons.summary: เด็ก decompensate ได้เร็วและ hypotension เป็น late sign. ใช้ appearance/work of breathing/circulation + primary assessment เพื่อตีความ physiology ก่อน diagnosis.

sections.title: 1) Pediatric Assessment Triangle
paragraphs: PAT = Appearance + Work of Breathing + Circulation to skin. เป็น rapid visual/auditory impression ไม่ต้องใช้อุปกรณ์ และช่วย classify respiratory distress/failure, shock or CNS/metabolic problem.

sections.title: 2) Primary assessment
paragraphs: A/B/C/D/E พร้อม age-appropriate vitals. HR/RR/BP ต้องตีความตามอายุและ context. Cap refill/peripheral pulse/mental status ช่วยเมื่อ BP ยังปกติ.
bullets: Hypotension = decompensated shock until proven otherwise
Bradycardia in sick child often points to hypoxia/late deterioration

sections.title: 3) Secondary assessment
paragraphs: SAMPLE + focused history: feeding/urine, fever, seizure, birth/prematurity, congenital heart disease, toxin/medication, trauma, immunization depending on case.

sections.title: 4) Reassessment
paragraphs: เด็กเปลี่ยนเร็ว จึงต้อง trend mental status, WOB, HR, perfusion, SpO₂, glucose and response to intervention rather than relying on one snapshot.

quick_review: Check glucose early in altered child

quiz.q: Hypotension ในเด็กมักเป็น early หรือ late sign ของ shock?
quiz.explain: Children can compensate with tachycardia/vasoconstriction until later decompensation.

lessons.title: Pediatric Arrest & Shock: ventilation-first physiology, epinephrine, defibrillation
lessons.summary: เด็ก arrest มักเริ่มจาก respiratory failure/shock. หัวใจของ PALS คือ prevention, ventilation/oxygenation, CPR quality, timely defibrillation และ weight-based dosing.

sections.title: 1) Arrest prevention
paragraphs: Recognize respiratory failure and shock before pulseless arrest. Correct hypoxia, support ventilation, obtain vascular access when needed and treat underlying cause.

sections.title: 2) CPR/defibrillation
paragraphs: Compression 100–120/min, depth ≥1/3 AP diameter. Shockable arrest: 2 J/kg → 4 J/kg → subsequent ≥4 J/kg up to 10 J/kg or adult dose.
bullets: Advanced airway: continuous compressions + breath every 2–3 s
Monitor EtCO₂ and invasive diastolic BP when available

sections.title: 3) Epinephrine & antiarrhythmics
paragraphs: Nonshockable pediatric arrest: initial epinephrine as early as possible. Shockable rhythm: prioritize defibrillation; epinephrine may be given after 2 shocks or earlier if rapid defibrillation is not possible.
bullets: Epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mg/mL), max 1 mg
Amiodarone 5 mg/kg or lidocaine 1 mg/kg for shock-refractory VF/pVT

sections.title: 4) Shock types
paragraphs: Hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic and obstructive shock require different resuscitation. Fluid volume/rate should reflect cause and response; cardiogenic shock can worsen with indiscriminate large boluses.

key_points: Early epinephrine matters in nonshockable arrest
Avoid routine calcium/bicarbonate unless special indication

research_updates.title: Earlier epinephrine in nonshockable pediatric arrest
research_updates.takeaway: Evidence updates identified observational studies linking shorter time to first epinephrine with better outcomes in nonshockable arrest; certainty remains limited.

research_updates.title: AHA/AAP PALS guideline refresh
research_updates.takeaway: The 2025 PALS guideline covers prearrest, arrest and post-arrest care, ventilation, drug/energy dosing, shock and arrhythmias across prehospital and hospital settings.

quiz.q: Initial nonshockable pediatric arrest: epinephrine timing?
quiz.explain: 2025 PALS supports early epinephrine for nonshockable arrest.
Routine calcium is not recommended except specific indications such as hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia or CCB overdose.

lessons.title: Pediatric Bradycardia, SVT & Wide-Complex Tachycardia
lessons.summary: Arrhythmia ในเด็กต้องเริ่มจาก perfusion/respiratory status. Bradycardia ส่วนใหญ่ secondary; tachycardia ต้องแยก sinus tachycardia, SVT และ wide-complex rhythms.

sections.title: 1) Bradycardia
paragraphs: Correct hypoxia/ventilation first. If HR <60/min with cardiopulmonary compromise despite effective ventilation with oxygen → start CPR. Epinephrine IV/IO if persistent after correction. Atropine for increased vagal tone/primary AV block.

sections.title: 2) SVT
paragraphs: SVT often regular narrow complex, abrupt onset, rate often very high for age. Stable → vagal then adenosine if access available. Unstable → synchronized cardioversion starting 0.5–1 J/kg, then 2 J/kg.

sections.title: 3) Wide-complex tachycardia
paragraphs: Consider VT vs SVT with aberrancy; if unstable cardiovert. Stable wide-complex requires expert guidance and careful drug selection; avoid reflex AV nodal blockade in pre-excitation contexts.

key_points: Unstable SVT/VT with pulse: synchronized cardioversion

quiz.q: Atropine เหมาะที่สุดใน pediatric brady แบบใด?
options: Increased vagal tone or primary AV block
quiz.explain: 2025 PALS limits atropine use to vagal tone/AV conduction block contexts rather than hypoxic bradycardia.

lessons.title: Pediatric Respiratory Distress & Failure
lessons.summary: เด็ก arrest มักเริ่มจาก respiratory failure: recognize compensation before bradycardia/hypotension.

sections.title: 1) Pediatric physiology
paragraphs: Higher metabolic demand, smaller airways and lower functional reserve mean deterioration can be rapid. Tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring and agitation are early; fatigue, poor effort, cyanosis and decreased consciousness suggest failure.

sections.title: 2) Upper vs lower vs lung tissue vs control
paragraphs: Stridor → upper airway; wheeze → lower airway; crackles/decreased compliance → lung tissue; irregular/slow breathing may reflect CNS or fatigue. Mixed disease is common.

sections.title: 3) Oxygenation and ventilation
paragraphs: SpO₂ alone can lag or mislead. Watch work of breathing, mental state, air movement and EtCO₂ when available.

sections.title: 4) Escalation
paragraphs: Position/suction, oxygen, bronchodilator/epinephrine when syndrome-appropriate, BVM support and advanced airway when ventilation cannot be maintained.

lessons.title: Pediatric Shock: Compensated First, Hypotensive Late
lessons.summary: tachycardia + perfusion abnormalities can be shock before BP falls.

sections.title: 1) Types
paragraphs: Hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic and obstructive shock all occur in children. History/exam and response to intervention guide phenotype.

sections.title: 2) Compensated shock
paragraphs: Tachycardia, cool or abnormal skin, prolonged capillary refill, weak peripheral pulses, narrow pulse pressure, irritability/lethargy may precede hypotension.

sections.title: 3) Fluids are not one-size-fits-all
paragraphs: Bolus volume and reassessment depend on condition. Myocarditis/cardiogenic shock and resource-limited septic contexts require special caution. Reassess lungs, liver, perfusion and BP after each bolus.

sections.title: 4) Deterioration
paragraphs: Bradycardia in a sick child often signals severe hypoxia/late decompensation; support ventilation aggressively.

lessons.title: Febrile Seizure: Simple vs Complex & Dangerous Mimics
lessons.summary: ชักร่วมไข้ส่วนใหญ่ benign แต่ต้องแยก prolonged/complex seizure และ CNS infection.

sections.title: 1) Typical simple febrile seizure
paragraphs: Generally generalized, brief, single episode in 24 h in a developmentally typical young child with fever; exact diagnostic age ranges follow pediatric guidance/local policy.

sections.title: 2) Complex/red flags
paragraphs: Focal features, prolonged duration, recurrence within 24 h, persistent altered mental status, meningismus, toxic appearance, age/context atypical or concern for CNS infection.

sections.title: 3) Immediate care
paragraphs: Protect from injury, airway positioning/suction, oxygen/ventilation as needed, check glucose, time seizure and treat prolonged seizure according to pediatric protocol.

sections.title: 4) Fever itself
paragraphs: Antipyretics may improve comfort but do not reliably prevent recurrence of febrile seizures.

lessons.title: Fever & Sepsis in Infants/Children
lessons.summary: appearance and age can matter more than the height of fever.

sections.title: 1) High-risk groups
paragraphs: Young infants, immunocompromised children, complex chronic disease and toxic/poor-appearing children need lower threshold for serious infection evaluation.

sections.title: 2) Pediatric sepsis phenotype
paragraphs: Abnormal perfusion, mental state, tachycardia, temperature abnormality and respiratory distress may precede hypotension.

sections.title: 3) Look for source but do not delay stabilization
paragraphs: Respiratory, urinary, CNS, skin/soft tissue and intra-abdominal sources are common.

sections.title: 4) EMS priorities
paragraphs: ABC, glucose, perfusion, temperature, appropriate oxygen/ventilation, IV/IO when indicated and early destination notification for shock.

lessons.title: Pediatric Asthma & Wheeze: Severity and Escalation
lessons.summary: wheeze in children has a broad differential; severe asthma is a clinical diagnosis of airflow failure.

sections.title: 1) Differential by age
paragraphs: Asthma, viral-induced wheeze/bronchiolitis, anaphylaxis, foreign body and structural airway problems can present with wheeze. Sudden unilateral wheeze/choking history raises foreign body concern.

sections.title: 2) Severity
paragraphs: Retractions, inability to speak/feed, agitation then fatigue, poor air entry, hypoxemia and altered consciousness indicate worsening severity.

sections.title: 3) Treatment principle
paragraphs: Inhaled bronchodilator is central for asthma; add systemic steroid and other adjuncts for moderate/severe disease according to protocol. IM epinephrine is for anaphylaxis rather than routine isolated asthma.

sections.title: 4) Impending failure
paragraphs: A tiring child with decreasing respiratory effort or bradycardia is an emergency—support ventilation and prepare advanced airway.

lessons.title: Pediatric Trauma: Anatomy, Compensation & Non-Accidental Injury
lessons.summary: children compensate differently and lose heat quickly; mechanism must be interpreted in context of development.

sections.title: 1) Anatomy/physiology
paragraphs: Larger head-to-body ratio, compliant chest wall, smaller circulating volume and high surface-area-to-mass ratio affect injury patterns and hypothermia risk.

sections.title: 2) Shock recognition
paragraphs: Hypotension is late. Tachycardia, skin/peripheral pulse changes and mental status are important early clues.

sections.title: 3) Airway/spine
paragraphs: Occiput and airway anatomy can complicate neutral positioning. Use pediatric equipment and age/size-appropriate techniques.

sections.title: 4) Safeguarding
paragraphs: Injury inconsistent with developmental ability, patterned injuries, changing stories or delay in care can suggest non-accidental trauma; document objectively and follow safeguarding pathways.
